cases.name: Marion Reid
cases.about:
Reid’s cousin, Destry Newsome said: Reid loved baseball, and she often watched the children play at the Chuckatuck Ballfield, giving dollars for home runs. 

“Yup, that she did,” Newsome said. “Every time, she would go around and give you a dollar. And when we used to play, sports names are here — baseball and basketball. She’s always out there cheering us on, and she was just a loving person.” Marion Reid’s rules included the rule: four fouls and you are out.  

She was so impactful in her community.   At the bottom of the flagpole at the Chuckatuck Sports League ballfield, there’s a memorial stone. It says: “Dedicated to the memory of Marion Reid: The Dollar Lady April 20, 1991.”  He adds: “She’d like to play cards. That was basically what she did, played cards and just like to see baseball, all kinds of sports, especially baseball. It was her thing. She loved it. She just loved to see the kids play baseball. She just loved when we tried out for a baseball team.” She was so impactful in her community.   At the bottom of the flagpole at the Chuckatuck Sports League ballfield, there’s a memorial stone. It says: “Dedicated to the memory of Marion Reid: The Dollar Lady April 20, 1991.”
cases.narrative: On 2/25/1990, she was found dead on the floor of her small semi-secluded home. Her last contact by phone was with family the day before. Marion was found bound with multiple injuries and had been sexually assaulted.
